trigger: The same person is signed in on the phone collector and on the web, for example a manager who also collects, or an observer who opens /o/<org>/collect or an invitation link. They press Sign out (header menu, Account > Security, or the delete-account page form), or 'Not you?' on /invite or /join.
current_behavior: GoTrue logout runs with scope 'global', which revokes every refresh token the user has. The web clears its cookies and redirects to /sign-in. The phone keeps its current access token until it expires; its next refresh then fails and the collector is signed out. The person's other web browsers are signed out too. The mobile app itself deliberately signs out with scope 'local' (mobile-inventory map, sign-out.tsx).
consequence: The web states something false about the record pipeline. The phone stops uploading until the observer signs in again, possibly in the field. Records stay on the device (owner_scope partition), so this is blocked sync and a broken promise, not record loss. The code comment shows the intent was this browser only.
smallest_fix: Pass { scope: 'local' } to supabase.auth.signOut() in lib/auth/actions.ts:138 and features/auth/actions.ts:127. If 'sign out everywhere' is ever wanted, make it a separate, explicitly worded control.
can_delete: Nothing.
guarantee_to_keep: Sign-out still clears this browser's Supabase and flow cookies and redirects. Account deletion keeps its local sign-out plus cookie wipe.
verification_scenario: Sign in as the same user in two browser contexts (or web plus simulator). Sign out in context A. In context B, call supabase.auth.refreshSession() (or wait past token expiry): B must stay signed in and the collector must still upload. The existing zones-account e2e (same-context tabs) must still see 'you were signed out' because the cookies are shared.
journey: Account / any workspace header -> Sign out; Invite/Join -> Not you?

trigger: Any navigation to Overview, Data, Observation, Sites, Site, Zones, the zone draft editor or publish, package inspect, or the form editor. warm-nav.json shows downloadPackageArchive on every soft navigation to these pages. The scaling trigger is a manager uploading a denser QGIS drawing that the API accepts.
current_behavior:
Nothing is reused across navigations. Each render downloads the archive from the API, runs unzipSync and JSON.parse synchronously on the Node event loop, projects every vertex to full-precision plan units, and serializes the ProjectedSite to client components (DataScreen, CoverageIsland, SiteScreen, and SitesScreen for up to 6 sites) in addition to the SVG. Lab archives cost 7-13 ms.

The reproducer (scratchpad/repro/siteplan-cost.mjs) runs the real readPackageArchive, packageSiteCollection and projectSite:
- Fall Creek's real layers, 10 KiB zip: 3 ms; 61 KiB projected JSON
- 832 KiB zip: 85 ms CPU; 5.6 MB projected JSON
- 7.9 MiB zip: 811 ms CPU; 55 MB projected JSON; process at 1.36 GB RSS
- next size up: Node crashed out of memory

The real survey drawings (Ithaca_QGIS/Drawings, 1,553 vertices) project to about 61 KB, so the pilot is far from the cliff.
consequence: At pilot scale there is no harm. A package of about 1 MiB would put about 6 MB of plan JSON plus SVG into each map page, multiplied up to 6 times on Sites. Around 8 MiB, each plan blocks the function for about a second and the page risks running out of memory. That site's web pages would become unusable while the API still calls the package ready.
smallest_fix: Add a byte budget in getSitePlan and getEditorBase, checking bytes.length before unzipSync. Over budget, return null so the existing planNote path says the plan is too detailed to draw on the web and to open it in QGIS. State the same limit once as an API preparation check. Round projected coordinates (for example 2 decimals in plan units) to roughly halve the payload. Only after real package sizes show a need, add a process-level cache of projected plans keyed by immutable package_id. Cache Components or 'use cache' are not justified for this.
can_delete: Nothing.
guarantee_to_keep: Each plan is still read through the viewer's own authorized archive request, keeps its historical binding (the record's own package version), and keeps the honest planNote when it cannot be drawn.
verification_scenario: Unit test: an archive over the budget makes getSitePlan return null without calling unzipSync, and the Data, Site and Sites pages show the note. Rerun siteplan-cost.mjs and compare projected JSON size after rounding. Re-measure cold.json 'zones' and 'sites' document sizes.
journey: Site plans across review pages
evidence_needed: Real package sizes from the pilot and other QGIS projects, and hosted function memory and time per map page.

check.checked: Confirmed in code: getPackageArchive (workspace.ts:227) uses React cache(), per request only; the API client fetches with cache:'no-store' and there is no cross-request cache. getSitePlan (:243-255) and getEditorBase (:261-277) run readPackageArchive (archive.ts:91-111: unzipSync of all entries, JSON.parse, zod, no size guard) and projectSite (plan.ts:536; toPlan :122-127 uses full doubles). All cited callers exist (CoverageSection:50, data/page:147, data/[observation]/page:41, sites/page:48, sites/[site]/page:56, zones/page:109, packages/page:135, forms/versions/[version]/page:121). Uncited callers also use it: zones/drafts/[draft]/page:103, publish/page:77 and loadSitePlanAction (features/data/actions.ts:101). Sites passes up to 6 plans (thumbnailSites limit 6) as props to client SitesScreen; DataScreen, CoverageIsland and SiteScreen are 'use client' too. warm-nav.json shows downloadPackageArchive on every relevant soft nav. I re-ran scratchpad/repro/siteplan-cost.mjs (real code): 10 KiB zip 2 ms/61 KiB JSON; 351 KiB 45 ms/2.5 MB; 923 KiB 99 ms/6.7 MB, RSS 432 MiB; 7.0 MiB 824 ms/58 MB, RSS 758 MiB; 14.0 MiB 1.9 s/116 MB, RSS 1.43 GB. Backend bounds: archive 16 MiB (packages.py:30), 20,000 features per layer, uploads up to 24 MiB, no vertex cap, so dense input is reachable by a manager. Real pilot data is about 10 KiB (Fall Creek) and 1,553 vertices (Ithaca survey).
check.correction: Mechanism and numbers reproduce, but the harm is hypothetical, so downgrade. (1) Category: MEASUREMENT NEEDED, since the finding's own evidence_needed is real package sizes, and pilot data sits about 4 orders below the problem range. (2) Severity: low at pilot scale. (3) Cost is linear (about 7x zip-to-JSON), not a cliff. (4) 'Next size up crashed Node OOM' did not reproduce: a 14 MiB zip finished in about 1.9 s at 1.43 GB RSS (no crash; depends on heap/host limits). The hosted memory risk is real only for multi-MiB packages, multiplied by up to 6 concurrent plans on Sites. (5) PlanZone also carries the raw lng/lat geometry next to projected parts, so rounding plan units alone will not halve zone-heavy payloads. (6) The proposed byte budget is new behavior for a hypothetical; reasonable, but defer until real sizes justify it. Not a compat or migration request, so not refuted on policy.

locations: web/src/features/forms/DraftEditorScreen.tsx:145-183 (save: start(async () => { await saveDraftAction(...) }) with no try/catch), :196-208 (startFromThis)
web/src/features/forms/PublishScreen.tsx:79, RetireDialog.tsx:37, DiscardDialog.tsx:41, NewFormDialog.tsx:79, FormVersionsScreen.tsx:100 (same pattern)
web/src/features/org/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx:98, TransferOwnership.tsx:58, features/org/projects/CreateProjectDialog.tsx:104, features/project-settings/SettingsScreen.tsx:120 (same pattern)
web/src/features/sites/EditSiteDialog.tsx:74-87, CreateSiteDialog.tsx:93, features/data/DataScreen.tsx:186-206 loadMore (try/finally without catch: no message shown)
web/src/proxy.ts:17,33-43 (protectedRoute && !authenticated -> NextResponse.redirect 307 for every method, including Server Action POSTs)

web/node_modules/next/dist/client/components/router-reducer/reducers/server-action-reducer.js:70-73 (fetch POST), :111-121 (a non-RSC response throws 'An unexpected response was received from the server.'), :302-305 (a network rejection is passed to reject(e))
web/node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/action-handler.js:127-206 createForwardedActionResponse (redirect:'manual', non-RSC result -> '{}' JSON)
web/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:5873-5897 chainThenableValue (a rejected transition thenable is thrown on render)
web/src/app/(app)/o/[org]/p/[project]/error.tsx:6-17 and web/src/components/shell/ErrorView.tsx:57-60 ('Something went wrong.' / 'Your records remain available.')
Correct pattern already in the repo: web/src/features/zones/StartDraft.tsx:64-75, DiscardDraft.tsx:64-70, features/data/DataMap.tsx:169-187
trigger: A manager has unsaved question edits in the form editor (it has no autosave; only Save draft writes). The iPad's Wi-Fi drops, the session has ended (signed out in another tab, or ended by the global sign-out in WDI-2), or a deploy happened since the page loaded. They press Save draft.
current_behavior: The Server Action promise rejects: the fetch throws, or the proxy 307s the POST to /sign-in and the forwarded action comes back as '{}' JSON, which is not an RSC response. The rejection happens inside a useTransition action, so React 19.2.4 throws it to the project error boundary. DraftEditorScreen unmounts, the leave guard goes with it, and ErrorView says 'Something went wrong. Your records remain available.' Its Try again rebuilds the editor from server props, so the edits are gone. The typed 'Nothing was saved. Sign in to continue.' path in forms/actions.ts:33-43 is never reached when the session has ended. In the site dialogs and in 'Show the next 500' the rejection is unhandled, and the button returns to normal with no message.
consequence: The manager loses form-draft work through ordinary network or session events, and the page gives no true reason. This breaks the 'a failed read/write says what did not happen' rule, and the zone editor already handles the same cases properly.
smallest_fix: Add one small helper, e.g. settleAction(promise, nothing), that turns a rejection into {status:'failed', message: UNCONFIRMED_CHANGE_COPY} (lib/api/errors.ts:293). Use it at the ~13 call sites listed. In proxy.ts, skip the sign-in redirect for non-GET/HEAD requests (or requests with a next-action header), so the action itself answers with its typed sign-in failure; ideally reword it as 'Sign in again in another tab, then save', as save-queue.ts:409 does. Keep the typed failures, the 'may have saved' honesty, the leave guard and the editor's in-memory state. Nothing needs deleting.
guarantee_to_keep: Protected document and RSC GETs still redirect to /sign-in?next=; the API still refuses unauthenticated writes; an unconfirmed write is never reported as success.
verification_scenario: Playwright with manager storage state: open forms/versions/<draft>, change a question's wording, call context.setOffline(true), click Save draft. Today ErrorView appears and, back online, the old wording returns. After the fix an attention Note with the unconfirmed copy appears, the edited wording is still in the fields, and going back online and pressing Save draft saves it. Repeat by signing out in a second page of the same context instead of going offline.

check.checked: Opened every cited site. DraftEditorScreen save (:143-183) and startFromThis (:196-209), PublishScreen :79, RetireDialog :37, DiscardDialog :41, NewFormDialog :79, FormVersionsScreen :100, org SettingsScreen :98, TransferOwnership :58, CreateProjectDialog :104 and project-settings SettingsScreen :120 all call start(async () => { await xAction(...) }) from useTransition with no try/catch. EditSiteDialog :74-87, CreateSiteDialog :92-116 and DataScreen.loadMore :186-206 use try/finally with no catch, so the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection and the busy flag resets with no message. In React 19.2.4, chainThenableValue (react-dom-client.development.js:5873) and updateTransition (:9022, useThenable) rethrow a rejected async transition at render. A react-test-renderer@19.2.4 reproducer (scratchpad/repro/v/transition-reject.cjs) showed the nearest error boundary rendering on rejection, and the component staying mounted with try/catch. In Next 16.2.7, server-action-reducer.js:69-73 does the POST fetch, :111-121 throws 'An unexpected response was received from the server.' for a non-RSC reply without x-action-redirect, and :302-305 calls reject(e). The only boundaries are app/(app)/o/[org]/p/[project]/error.tsx, [org]/error.tsx and global-error.tsx; ErrorView shows 'Something went wrong.' / 'Your records remain available.' and Try again (unstable_retry) remounts from server props. The forms feature has no autosave or storage, and the service worker (service-worker.js:82) ignores non-GET, so an offline POST really rejects. proxy.ts:17,33-43 issues NextResponse.redirect (default 307, response.js:99) for every method under /o and /account. action-handler.js:456-466 and :127-206 forward the action to a worker that has it, with redirect:'manual', and a non-RSC result becomes '{}' JSON. That session-ended chain is code-traced only, not run. Correct patterns confirmed at zones/StartDraft.tsx:64-75, DiscardDraft.tsx:58-75, DataMap.tsx:165-187 and zones/editor/save-queue.ts:409. No code or test already guards the form editor. WDI-3 and WDI-2 are separate findings.
check.correction: The core claim holds: a rejected Server Action inside start(async ...) throws to the project error boundary and discards unsaved form-editor edits, and the try/finally sites fail silently. Three corrections. (1) Severity is medium, not high. The loss is limited to edits since the last manual Save, the trigger is transient (offline at the moment of Save, session ended), nothing server-side is corrupted, and the manager can redo the edits. (2) The smallest_fix is wrong about the copy. If proxy.ts merely stops redirecting non-GET requests, a signed-out action reaches resolveProject, then getWorkspace 'unauthenticated', then workspaceError, which builds an ApiError with no status. failedChange then calls failedWrite, and wasRefused(status undefined) is false, so the message is UNCONFIRMED_CHANGE_COPY ('could not confirm the change. Reload the page...'), not 'Nothing was saved. Sign in to continue.'. That copy only appears on a real API 401 with a status. The copy needs its own sign-in wording such as save-queue.ts:409's 'Sign in again in another tab, then come back to save', and 'Reload the page' is bad advice here because a document GET redirects to sign-in and drops the edits. (3) The ~13 call sites count is roughly right (14 by my count). The settleAction helper plus the proxy tweak is a sound minimal design. The offline and 5xx/413 triggers are the strongest evidence. The session-ended chain through the forwarded-action '{}' response is only code-traced.

title: Web Sign out is global: it ends the person's collector session on every phone, while the Account page says it does not affect the app
journey: Observer or manager who also collects; invitation 'Not you?' on a shared laptop; sign out from the account menu or the Account page
locations: web/src/lib/auth/actions.ts:136-146 signOut (supabase.auth.signOut() with no scope, :138)
web/src/features/auth/actions.ts:124-133 switchAccount ('Not you?', :127 same call)

web/src/features/account/SecurityIsland.tsx:23 footnote 'Signing out here does not affect the app...'; :50 sign-out form; components/shell/AccountMenu.tsx:47,120; features/account/DeleteAccount.tsx:150
web/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.117.2/node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/main/GoTrueClient.js:3384-3398,3417,3427 (default scope 'global': 'signs the user out of every device')

mobile/src/auth/provider.tsx:89,129 (the collector itself uses scope 'local'); mobile/src/auth/session-retention.ts:19-24 (an unexpected SIGNED_OUT keeps the account but leaves no session); mobile/PLAN.md:126 lists 'global sign-out' as a cause of revocation
trigger: Someone signed in on the collector signs out on the web. Or on a shared lab laptop an RA opens their invitation link, sees the PI signed in, and presses 'Not you?', which ends the PI's sessions everywhere.
current_behavior: Supabase revokes every refresh token for that user. The phone keeps working until its access token expires (about 1 h). Then its refresh fails, supabase-js emits SIGNED_OUT, and the collector has no session: uploads stop until the person signs in again with their password on the device.
consequence: Collection in the field is blocked unexpectedly (records are kept by the mobile retention code, so nothing is lost), and the Account page states the opposite. The same global sign-out also ends any open web editor sessions on other machines, which then hits WDI-1.
smallest_fix: Pass { scope: 'local' } in signOut (lib/auth/actions.ts:138) and in switchAccount (features/auth/actions.ts:127). Two lines; after this the existing copy is true. Keep the flow-cookie deletion and the redirect.
guarantee_to_keep: Signing out on the web still clears this browser's session and auth-flow cookies and purges the router cache; account deletion keeps its existing local sign-out.
verification_scenario: Locally, sign the same account into the iOS simulator collector and the web. Sign out on the web, then force a token refresh on the device (foreground the app after the access-token lifetime, or set a short JWT expiry in local Supabase). Before the fix the device shows signed out and uploads pause; after the fix the device stays signed in and uploads. Add a unit/e2e check that the action calls signOut with scope 'local'.

check.checked: web/src/lib/auth/actions.ts:136-146 signOut calls supabase.auth.signOut() with no scope (:138), and features/auth/actions.ts:124-133 switchAccount does the same (:127). The installed @supabase/auth-js 2.117.2 GoTrueClient.js:3417 defaults to scope 'global', and its doc comment at :3384-3398 says this 'signs the user out of every device'. @supabase/ssr 0.12.7 does not override the scope. The only web caller using 'local' is account deletion (features/account/actions.ts:103). The copy SecurityIsland.tsx:23 ('Signing out here does not affect the app...') contradicts this. Callers confirmed: SecurityIsland.tsx:50, AccountMenu.tsx:47,120 and DeleteAccount.tsx:150, the last in the deletion-finishing state where global is harmless. Mobile deliberately uses scope 'local' (provider.tsx:89,129; mobile/PLAN.md:242,264). PLAN.md:126 names 'global sign-out' as a cause of supabase-js deleting the session. session-retention.ts:19-24 keeps the account and nulls the session on an unexpected SIGNED_OUT. gate.tsx decideGate sets signedIn = session || cachedAccount and authOpen = !session, so the app stays in the 'app' route. SessionBanner and ResumeUploadsNote show 'Sign in to resume uploads'. The backend verifies JWTs locally via JwksVerifier (backend/src/fieldmaps_api/auth.py), so the phone keeps working until its access token expires (about 1 h). Not run end to end (no servers or devices).
check.correction: The core claim is confirmed: web Sign out and 'Not you?' revoke every session for that user, which contradicts the Account page footnote. The consequence is overstated. Collection is not blocked: the cached account keeps the gate on the app route, and records and local collection continue. What stops is uploads, after the access token lapses (about 1 h) and the refresh fails. The app shows 'Sign in to resume uploads', and the fix is the person re-entering their password on the device, so it is recoverable and loses nothing. Severity is medium, not high. It is reachable by an ordinary user with one account on web and phone, and by the shared-laptop 'Not you?' case. The two-line fix ({ scope: 'local' } at lib/auth/actions.ts:138 and features/auth/actions.ts:127) is correct and is not a backward-compatibility request.

title: Open redirect after sign-in: safeNext turns dot-segment paths into '//evil.com'
journey: Sign in / sign up / verify / reset password with a ?next= link
locations: web/src/lib/auth/navigation.ts:4-17 safeNext (checks raw and decoded startsWith('//') before normalising, then returns url.pathname + url.search at :13)
web/src/app/(auth)/(signed-out)/sign-in/page.tsx:18-19,30 -> web/src/features/auth/SignInForm.tsx:59 hidden input -> web/src/lib/auth/actions.ts:41,93,133 redirect(next)
web/node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/action-handler.js:240 (x-action-redirect: //evil.com)
web/node_modules/next/dist/client/assign-location.js (new URL('//evil.com', href) = https://evil.com/) and server-action-reducer.js:215-227 (isExternalURL -> completeHardNavigation)
web/tests/auth.test.mjs:8-22 (tests cover '//', '/\\', '%2f%2f' and '%5c' only)
trigger: An attacker sends https://<web>/sign-in?next=/a/..//evil.example. The manager signs in on the real site with the real password.
current_behavior: Reproduced with the real function (scratchpad/repro/safenext-test.mjs): '/a/..//evil.com' -> '//evil.com', '/.//evil.com' -> '//evil.com', '/%2e%2e//evil.com' -> '//evil.com', '/o/..//evil.com/x' -> '//evil.com/x'. authenticate redirects to that value. The Next client resolves it against the page URL to https://evil.com/ and does a hard navigation.
consequence: A credible phishing step: right after a real sign-in the researcher lands on an attacker page (for example a fake 'session expired, sign in again').
smallest_fix: In safeNext, after new URL(value, base), return HOME unless url.origin equals the base origin and !url.pathname.startsWith('//'). Add the four cases above to tests/auth.test.mjs. About two lines plus tests; nothing to delete.
guarantee_to_keep: Internal paths and queries are kept; auth pages and anything unparsable still go to /o.
verification_scenario: Unit: each case above returns '/o', and '/account?tab=profile' is unchanged. Manual: open /sign-in?next=/a/..//example.com, sign in, and land on /o.

check.checked: I ran the real safeNext (web/src/lib/auth/navigation.ts via node --experimental-strip-types). One pass does return '//evil.com' for '/a/..//evil.com', '/.//evil.com' and '/%2e%2e//evil.com', and '//evil.com/x' for '/o/..//evil.com/x'. I then traced every sink that reaches redirect(). Each auth page runs safeNext first (sign-in/page.tsx:19, sign-up:19, verify:23, forgot-password:25, reset-password:53) and passes the result as the hidden input name='next' (SignInForm.tsx:59, SignUpForm:73, VerifyForm:69, ForgotPasswordForm:54, ResetPasswordForm:69). The authenticate action then runs safeNext(form.get('next')) again (lib/auth/actions.ts:41) before redirect(next) at :93 and :133. The second pass sees '//evil.com', hits value.startsWith('//'), and returns '/o'. Simulating the chain (repro/v/sn3.mjs) gives page '//evil.com' and action '/o' for all four attack strings. A 500k-input fuzz (repro/v/sn4.mjs) found 2141 one-pass external results and 0 two-pass external results. Other sinks cannot reach another origin. switchAccount (features/auth/actions.ts:125-132) always redirects to /sign-in?next=<encoded>. AccountChip's hidden next is an invitation path or '/o', SecurityIsland's is a constant '/account', and the forgot-password and sign-up redirects encode next into /reset-password or /verify. Only a forged direct POST to the Server Action would see single-pass output, and Next's Origin-versus-Host check on Server Actions plus the need for the victim's credentials rule that out as an ordinary-user path. The finding's own manual check (open /sign-in?next=/a/..//example.com, sign in, land on /o) already passes today.
check.correction: The stated exploit does not work. The finding's reproducer applied safeNext once, but the sign-in page and the authenticate action each apply it, so the dot-segment output '//evil.com' is re-sanitized to '/o' before redirect(). There is no reachable open redirect and no phishing consequence. What remains is a latent weakness: safeNext is not idempotent or origin-safe on its own, and tests/auth.test.mjs never exercises the dot-segment cases. Hardening safeNext (reject any result that starts with '//' or whose origin differs) plus the four test cases is cheap defense in depth, but it is a low-severity hygiene change, not a high-severity defect, and it should be dropped from the confirmed-defect list.

title: Installed web app opened offline shows the public landing page ('Sign in') instead of saying it needs a connection; legacy cache names remain
journey: Manager opens the installed DECA Mark app on a laptop or iPad without a connection
locations: web/src/lib/pwa/service-worker.js:20-24 installStartUrl, :84-85, :96-99 (offline /o navigation -> cache.match('/'))
web/src/app/manifest.ts:9 (start_url '/o')
web/src/app/(marketing)/page.tsx:33-57 (Sign in / Create account calls to action)
web/src/lib/pwa/service-worker.js:2-4,65 (LEGACY_CACHE 'fieldmaps-shell-v1', LEGACY_PREFIX 'fieldmaps-public-', kept from the rename in 52f6267)
trigger: Launch the installed app while offline.
current_behavior: The service worker answers /o with the cached marketing landing page, which offers Sign in and Create account. That suggests the person is signed out, and both buttons fail offline. README:134 does not mention it.
consequence: A misleading state rather than an honest 'no connection'. It does no harm to data: nothing authenticated is cached.

guarantee_to_keep: Only '/', /icons/* and /_next/static/* are ever stored; RSC, Authorization, private/no-store and redirected responses are never stored.
verification_scenario: On an https preview, install the app, switch DevTools to offline and open /o: after the fix no landing page appears. Check that the Cache Storage keys contain only decamark-public-<build>.

title: Any schema-version mismatch silently drops every unsent observation, draft and package file at app start
locations: mobile/src/storage/database-migrations.ts:5 SCHEMA_VERSION
mobile/src/storage/database-migrations.ts:55-89 initializeDatabase (check :61, drop loop :69-79)
mobile/src/storage/database-migrations.ts:8-53 resetSchema (marker insert :52)
mobile/src/storage/initialize-collector.ts:9-18 initializeCollectorDatabase
mobile/src/packages/hosted/device.ts:132-136 resetHostedPackages
mobile/app/_layout.tsx:105-108 SQLiteProvider onInit
mobile/src/auth/account-summaries.ts:10-11,64-84 readAccountSummaries
trigger: Installing any build whose SCHEMA_VERSION differs from the one on the device. That is either an update that bumps it or an older build, because the check is `user_version === SCHEMA_VERSION`. git: the version went 4->5 on 2026-10-11 (a86a1ee) and 5->6 on 2026-10-13 (4eaf103). Janet began using the collector on 2026-10-08 (decisions D27).
current_behavior: This runs behind the Suspense splash, before any screen exists. In one transaction it drops every table, including pending, needs-attention and local-only observations, active and parked drafts, and grants. It then recreates the schema, sets package_files_need_reset and deletes Documents/hosted. There is no count, no prompt and no log. Repro: scratchpad/repro/mobile-records/reset-repro.ts runs the real initializeDatabase on node:sqlite. A v5 database with 2 unsent records and 1 draft ends with 0 observations, 0 drafts and the marker set to '1'. reset-downgrade-repro.ts (user_version 7, i.e. installing an older build) gives the same result. Welcome summaries for signed-out accounts (accounts/{id}.json) survive and keep announcing 'N records waiting' that no longer exist.
consequence: A routine update destroys unsent field observations the server never received, for every account on the device. This breaks PRODUCT.md:23 'Never lose a record' and :173 'A record survives a force quit, a restart…'. The pilot is imminent and the bump cadence is days.
smallest_fix: Keep the reset, as the policy allows, but refuse it when it would destroy unsent work. Inside the existing transaction, before dropping anything, count unsent observations (sync_state <> 'synced') plus active and parked drafts, tolerating missing tables. If the count is above 0, roll back and throw a typed error that the root ErrorBoundary shows as a blocking screen: 'This version cannot open N observations saved by the previous version. Do not delete the app. Install the previous version again, let them upload, then update.' Reset silently only when nothing is unsent. On reset, also delete the stale accounts/*.json summaries. No migration code.
verification_scenario: Unit test: a v5 database with one pending row makes initializeDatabase reject, the row is still present and hosted/ is untouched. A database holding only synced rows resets. On a device: install build N, save a record offline, install N+1 with a bumped version. You should see the blocking screen with the record intact. Reinstall N and the record uploads.
can_delete: Nothing extra is needed. No migration ladder is added.
guarantee_to_keep: Pre-launch resets stay allowed whenever the device holds no unsent work. The transactional drop with rollback and the durable package-file marker stay.
evidence_needed: None for the defect itself. How often pilot builds ship decides how likely it is.
journey: An observer installs a new build mid-pilot with records still on the device.

check.checked: Read database-migrations.ts (SCHEMA_VERSION=6 at :5, strict === check at :61, drop loop :69-79, marker :52), initialize-collector.ts:13-17, device.ts:132-136 (ROOT='hosted'), _layout.tsx:105-108, account-summaries.ts (reads files only, so stale counts survive). Re-ran reset-repro.ts and reset-downgrade-repro.ts with Node 24: 2 unsent + 1 draft become 0 observations, 0 drafts, marker '1'. No logging in these files. Read docs/plan/README.md:10-14 'Pre-launch compatibility policy (2026-10-11)', PACKAGE-LIFECYCLE.md:3,7, mobile/README.md:28,314, PLAN.md:294,331, the database-migrations tests, docs/plan/current-state.md, decisions.md D27, and the no-legacy-support memory. Checked git history of SCHEMA_VERSION.
check.correction: The mechanism is exactly as described, but it is a deliberate, documented, tested pre-launch policy, not an accidental defect. docs/plan/README.md:10-14 says there are no real users or production-data preservation obligations, that breaking changes may reset incompatible local data, and not to add old-schema upgrade paths to retain experimental data. The tests 'Prelaunch collection schema reset' assert populated tables end at 0. current-state.md (2026-10-15) says this is 'not pilot readiness', with physical-device acceptance pending. D27 is a plan decision ('Janet starts using the collector on 2026-10-08'), not evidence that real unsent records are on devices, so 'mid-pilot' and 'critical' are not supported today. Git correction: a86a1ee (2026-10-11) went 3 to 5, not 4 to 5, and the same commit deleted the v1-v3 migration ladder and the NewerDatabaseError downgrade guard on purpose. 4eaf103 (2026-10-13) 5 to 6 is correct. The proposed guard is not a migration, so it is not refuted on policy grounds. It would also block the owner's own routine dev resets whenever test records exist. Reframe as a pilot-freeze gate: before real observers' unsent records live on tablets, a schema mismatch must refuse to wipe unsent rows and drafts. It becomes high or critical from that point. Also delete accounts/*.json summaries on reset. Keep severity medium and category DESIGN PREFERENCE until then.

title: Account, sign-out and delete-account say the app cannot upload, and one stored state carries three names

mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/account/sign-out.tsx:126-129

mobile/src/features/preview/queue.ts:9-14 STATUS_TO_STATE (pending->onDevice, local-only->held)

Under the stated reset policy the key can be removed with a schema bump and reset.

The 4-field key with 3 dead fields and the constant-versus-constant issuer checks are real complexity, but the finding's 'guard first, then delete' ordering is a data-preservation ask the Oct 11 policy does not require.
